statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-77524 (GHSA-637c-6jxx-4rwm) is privilege escalation when the KEDA operator resolves TriggerAuthentication credentials (for example unvalidated HashiCorp Vault address handling) while reconciling ScaledObjects. This image ships only the external metrics adapter built from cmd/adapter, which serves custom metrics via pkg/metricsservice and pkg/provider over gRPC to the operator. The Go module graph for that build still links pkg/scaling/resolver transitively, but inspection of the shipped keda-adapter binary shows only resolver package init/data symbols and no ResolveAuthRef, resolveAuthRef, NewHashicorpVaultHandler, Initialize, or ResolveSecrets method symbols from the HashicorpVaultHandler path described in GHSA-637c-6jxx-4rwm, so the vulnerable credential-resolution functions are not present in the executable.

CVE-2026-77524 (GHSA-637c-6jxx-4rwm) is privilege escalation when the KEDA operator resolves TriggerAuthentication credentials (for example unvalidated HashiCorp Vault address handling) while reconciling ScaledObjects. This image ships only the external metrics adapter built from cmd/adapter, which serves custom metrics via pkg/metricsservice and pkg/provider over gRPC to the operator. The Go module graph for that build still links pkg/scaling/resolver transitively, but inspection of the shipped keda-adapter binary shows only resolver package init/data symbols and no ResolveAuthRef, resolveAuthRef, NewHashicorpVaultHandler, Initialize, or ResolveSecrets method symbols from the HashicorpVaultHandler path described in GHSA-637c-6jxx-4rwm, so the vulnerable credential-resolution functions are not present in the executable.

CVE-2026-77524 is a privilege-escalation issue in the KEDA operator: a namespace tenant can steer TriggerAuthentication HashiCorp Vault authentication so the operator sends its cluster-privileged ServiceAccount token to a tenant-controlled URL during ScaledObject scaler reconciliation (fixed in KEDA v2.21.0 per GitHub Security Advisory). This image builds and ships only the keda-admission-webhooks binary from cmd/webhooks, which serves validating admission webhooks for KEDA CRDs and does not run operator reconciliation, scaler authentication, or outbound Vault login with the operator identity.

CVE-2026-53572 affects github.com/kedacore/keda/v2 at version 2.19.0 and is fixed in 2.20.0. This vulnerability is in the keda core code itself, not a dependency. The keda-admission-webhooks binary is built from the keda source repository at a specific version tag. Fixing this CVE in the 2.19 track would require upgrading to keda 2.20.x, which is a major version change that may introduce breaking changes. Users requiring the fix should use the 2.20 track images, which are already built from keda v2.20.1 and do not exhibit this vulnerability.

The fix version (v2.20.0) introduces incompatible transitive dependencies (sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime v0.19.7) that cause compilation failures with kserve v0.19.0. Upgrading requires either a newer kserve version or finding a compatible keda version that addresses the CVE.
